newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS SEEN DAZED BY DUTCH RATE HIKE TALK.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS SEEN DAZED BY DUTCH RATE HIKE TALK.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) ended flat to lower on Monday and dealers said the short-term outlook was also bearish with talk of a Dutch rate hike and other factors clouding the horizon.

"I think if the Dutch hike, Belgium will follow," one trader said in response to rumours the Dutch central bank will raise rates after its next policy meeting on Thursday to counter a weakening of the guilder and to calm money market rates.
But he noted that if the Belgians do not follow, this could help the OLO market. The Belgian National Bank's central rate is presently at 3.00 percent. The Dutch equivalent is at 2.50%.
The Belgian franc recovered from recent lows against the mark on Monday, rising to 20.6384/94 from 20.6410/20.

The rumours about a Dutch rate hike coincided with an interview given by Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse in which he told the Luxemburger Wort newspaper European interest rates were already low enough.

Another dealer said the market was also awaiting news on German inflation, with initial reports on West German CPI due from Tuesday, and a hint from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on the direction of U.S. interest rates. Greenspan is due to speak in Congress on both Wednesday and Thursday.

Monday's business was dominated by the Belgian Treasury's monthly OLO auction, in which the Treasury sold 10.025 billion francs of the 10-year benchmark OLO 26 (6.25 percent, March 2007) and 3.8 billion francs of OLO 10 (8.75 percent, June 2002), which some see destined to become the new five-year benchmark. The thin volumes did not surprise players.

One trader said OLO 10 was already a very liquid bond and there was not real demand for the paper because of its high coupon. "You have to pay too much over par," he said. He hoped the Treasury would launch a new 5-year bond with a coupon more in line with present market rates.
Another trader said, however, that OLO 10 was too far away at the moment for a five-year benchmark and he did not expect the Treasury to launch any new paper in that area of the curve.

"If they are going to start a new line I think it will be at the very long end - the OLO 16 (7.50 percent, July 2008) area. There will be need for another one there. OLO 16 is getting near to the 10-years," he said.

A Treasury decision to allow the 10-year benchmark OLO 26 to be stripped from Tuesday would also spark a limited reaction, traders said. "If people want this I haven't heard about it," said one domestic primary dealer.

OLO 26 will become the fourth bond to have its interest and principal separately traded, but the first 10-year benchmark to be stripped. The trader said the strips market had so far proved limited to trading in bonds' principals rather than coupons.

The yield on OLO 26 ended at 5.65 percent, up from 5.62 percent on Friday night and unchanged from its level at Monday's auction. The spread over Bunds was steady at 10 basis points. The spread could temporarily edge out if the Belgian National Bank hiked rates with the Dutch, one trader said.
